prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: six-frame game-player dancing spritesheet.
Primary request: generate a player dancing spritesheet on tile.

The sole supplied image is an authored SVG raster geometry and pose guide. Convert each stick figure to one finished player character. Invent anatomy and costume detail; do not copy stick strokes. The green squares establish scale and the fixed projected ground location. Produce exactly SIX DISTINCT poses in three columns and two rows, row-major, matching the six isolated guide panels.

Character identity in every panel: a cheerful young adult game player with warm skin, short thick tousled dark-brown hair, expressive brown eyes, coral-red open casual jacket, cream shirt, dark navy trousers, and cream low-top sneakers. Clean polished 2D game illustration, clear outlines, readable forms, modest soft shading. Keep face, outfit, colors, proportions, character scale, camera and lighting consistent.

POSE INSTRUCTIONS — left/right in this list mean the viewer's IMAGE-LEFT and IMAGE-RIGHT sides, exactly as seen in the stick guide, not anatomical labels. Six distinct poses are required:
1. TOP LEFT: both elbows bent outward and hands around shoulder height; knees gently bent, centered stance.
2. TOP MIDDLE: torso leans toward image-left, IMAGE-LEFT ARM RAISED above the head, image-right arm extended lower; weight shifts left.
3. TOP RIGHT: torso leans toward image-right, IMAGE-RIGHT ARM RAISED above the head, image-left arm extended lower; weight shifts right.
4. BOTTOM LEFT: BOTH HANDS OVERHEAD, elbows open, clearly wide stance, knees bent.
5. BOTTOM MIDDLE: IMAGE-RIGHT ARM RAISED, IMAGE-LEFT ARM LOW and down toward image-left. A crossed dance step: the leg and shoe arriving from image-left cross IN FRONT toward image-right, the other leg behind. Slight image-left hip sway.
6. BOTTOM RIGHT: IMAGE-LEFT ARM RAISED, IMAGE-RIGHT ARM LOW and down toward image-right. The OPPOSITE crossed step: the leg and shoe arriving from image-right cross IN FRONT toward image-left, the other leg behind. Slight image-right hip sway.
The final pair must visibly differ in BOTH raised-arm direction and which leg crosses in front. Do not repeat frame 5 in frame 6. Preserve the pose order; no repeated holds. Follow the guide's arm directions precisely.

Geometry: preserve reference canvas ratio 640:672, preferably output 1600×1680 pixels or equivalent proportional size. Reference panel size is 192×320, columns start x=0,224,448, rows start y=0,352; gutters are 32px. Keep all gutters genuinely alpha transparent, with no character, floor or effects crossing into them. Every head, hair, hand, arm, leg and shoe stays wholly inside its own panel with safe margins.

In each panel retain one flat screen-aligned square at reference coordinates x=32..160,y=184..312. Its center (96,248) is the character's projected ground position throughout the dance. Foot crossing changes the pose, not the floor's placement or the fixed ground point. Shoe toes may reach below this center. Keep the square plain, solid RGB 123,209,75, with straight edges, no rim, wall, perspective tilt, texture, accents, gradient, outline or cast shadow. Reserve this green hue for the square; no green character parts.

Real alpha transparency everywhere outside character and green square. No painted checkerboard, opaque black/white backdrop, grid, labels, text, borders, watermark, scenery, props, extra characters, particles or glow. Return one complete six-panel spritesheet.

retryReason: The first generated final pair repeated the raised-arm direction instead of following the opposite guide poses.
